The second-year defensive back was responsible for perhaps the biggest play of the game, as his strip sack of the Dolphins' Kyle McCord early in the third quarter led to a fumble recovery in the end zone by teammate Adetomiwa Adebawore. Walley was named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week for his big performance.

Allen led the Colts in tackles Sunday, and he got to Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord for an eight-yard loss late in the fourth quarter. Allen also picked off McCord earlier in the fourth, although the play was nullified by an illegal contact penalty by Colts defensive back Kenneth Harris. Allen has logged at least 10 tackles in each of his last three outings, and he has accumulated 34 tackles (12 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses across seven regular-season games.

Carlies hurt his neck in Week 9 against Dallas and didn't practice at all last week before being ruled out for Sunday's win over the Dolphins. Now that he's landed on IR, the third-year linebacker will need to miss at least the Colts' next four games. Austin Ajiake and West Weeks will likely soak up the rotational defensive snaps that Carlies had been getting.

injuries.detail: Davis-Gaither was already ruled out for Sunday's game against Miami in what would be his second consecutive missed contest due to a knee injury. Now that he's been placed on IR, the seventh-year pro will be required to miss at least four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 20.

Key missed the Colts' last five games while on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 4 against the Commanders. He was cleared to return to practice Wednesday and logged a trio of full sessions, which gave the Colts the confidence to activate the veteran defensive lineman from IR ahead of Sunday's contest. Prior to his IR stint, Key posted eight tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one forced fumble in four regular-season games.

Green has strung together six consecutive full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He's not quite ready to be activated from IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 29. Green is in the final stages of his recovery from an elbow injury that he suffered in Week 1 against the Browns.

Striggow entered the league's concussion protocol following the Jaguars' Week 10 win over the Titans. He was limited in all three practice sessions during Week 11 prep, and he would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear protocol and be available for Sunday's contest. Bryan Thomas and Wesley Williams would both see a bump in rotational snaps at defensive end if Striggow is inactive.

Walker was a full participant in Friday's practice, and that was enough for the fifth-year defensive end to avoid an injury tag heading into Sunday's contest. The 2022 first-rounder has 22 tackles (10 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and two pass defenses through nine regular-season games.

Johnson was a limited participant in all three Week 11 practices, but the 2023 fifth-rounder has done enough to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. Johnson has accumulated 40 tackles (23 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense across eight regular-season games.
Allen has next to no fantasy appeal having played a total of 73 offensive snaps this season. In nine games, he's touched the ball a total of three times on offense.

The backup running back has been dealing with the hand issue for weeks but continues to play through it. Rodriguez has averaged an underwhelming 3.9 yards per carry on 59 attempts this season, allowing Bhayshul Tuten to run away with lead-back duties in Jacksonville.

Tuten was limited at practice Wednesday, listed as a 'DNP' on Thursday, and then returned to a limited session Friday as he continues to manage the ankle and toe issues he has played through over the last two weeks. Also cleared to play versus New York were fellow RBs Chris Rodriguez (hand) and LeQuint Allen (hamstring), but Tuten nonetheless remains the clear top option in Jacksonville's backfield on the heels of recording a 70 percent snap share en route to carrying 26 times for 88 yards and a TD, to go along with three catches on four targets for 25 yards, in last weekend's 40-23 win over the Titans.

Meyers has been playing through the ankle injury for weeks, so his status was never in real doubt despite limited practices all week. The veteran wideout doesn't have a touchdown catch since Week 3 and has topped 65 receiving yards in a game just once all season. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option.

Jonah Monheim will draw the start at center in place of Hainsey, who exited this past Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans due to a knee sprain, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. According to Fowler, Hainsey's knee injury isn't considered season-ending, but the veteran lineman is viewed as week-to-week and could be a candidate for injured reserve.

Sunday was the third time in nine regular-season games that Oluokun played every single defensive snap and the second time that he reached double-digit tackles. His nine solo stops were a season high and most in a game since Week 1 of the 2024 season. Oluokun has accumulated 44 tackles (30 solo), including 2.0 sacks, over his last five outings.

Little was able to make four field-goal tries for the second straight week, converting attempts from 46, 48, 36 and 40 yards in the contest. The kicker has now gone 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests during the 2026 campaign.

Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. Hunter's impact on both sides of the ball has been undeniable: he has 28 catches (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and a touchdown, along with 36 tackles (24 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions) through nine regular-season games. The Jaguars will hit the road for Week 11 against the Giants on Nov. 22.

Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.

The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. Lawrence will take a sharp 21:5 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Giants.

The Jaguars keep blowing out their opponents, and Strange contributed a three-yard touchdown Sunday but was otherwise not heard from much, as Parker Washington dog-walked the Titans' secondary for 7-152-1 receiving on nine targets. Strange's touchdown grab was his first since Week 1. He remans a locked-in TE1 for fantasy, as he is playing virtually every snap in an elite offense.

Norman-Lott was removed from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday, but he may not be ready to make his 2026 regular-season debut as he continues to work his way back from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025. His return would give the Chiefs more depth on the interior defensive line behind starters Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga.

Moore will miss a second consecutive game due to an ankle injury, which means Joshua Ezeudu will likely start at right tackle against Arizona. Moore's next chance to play is Week 12 against Buffalo on Thanksgiving Day.

Smith entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons. He was unable to practice all week, and his absence means Mike Caliendo will likely start at right guard Sunday. Smith's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bills on Thanksgiving Day.

Kelce was forced from last Sunday's game against the Falcons with the ankle injury, but he's good to go for Week 11 against a hapless Arizona squad. The Chiefs should run all over the Cardinals' defense and likely won't need much pass volume from Patrick Mahomes. Kelce is more of a fringe TE1 for fantasy purposes.

There was no sense in pushing Walker to play against a Cardinals team that is injury-ruined and likely to be blown out at Arrowhead. Johnson will get another crack at RB1 duties after he dismantled Atlanta's defense for 171 total yards and two touchdowns on 28 touches last Sunday. He's a top-five fantasy RB1 play.
questionable

Walker, who wasn't able to practice this week, will thus target a potential return Thursday against the Bills. With the Chiefs erring on the side of caution with Walker with a short week ahead, Emmett Johnson -- who rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and TDs in the team's Week 10 win over the Falcons -- is headed toward a second consecutive start this weekend.

Bolton popped up on the Chiefs' injury report with a shin issue Wednesday, but it doesn't look like it was anything serious. He's fifth in the league in total tackles (89) going into a Week 11 matchup versus a pass-happy Cardinals offense.

Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

Tranquill finished tied for the team lead in tackles with fellow linebacker Nick Bolton in Week 10, notching at least nine takedowns for the third time in four weeks after not having reached that mark in any of the team's first five games of the year. On the season, Tranquill has now produced 75 total tackles (39 solo), two passes defensed and a fumble recovery over nine contests so far.

Williams was able to register at least five takedowns for the third time this season, and his biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he intercepted a deep pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix. The interception was his second of the year, and he has now compiled 41 total tackles (23 solo) and 11 passes defensed over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Briningstool connected with Patrick Mahomes for a 20-yard reception midway through the first quarter but didn't record another reception. The 23-year-old tight end has exactly one catch in each of his past three games. That's not enough production to warrant fantasy consideration, but Briningstool is at least showing growth as a pass catcher, as he had just one catch on two targets over his first six contests of the campaign.
Butker did not attempt a field goal in the contest, as the Chiefs solely scored touchdowns. He now moves to 27-for-28 on PATs in 2026 as he continues to struggle to hold onto the starting kicker job.

Gray was unable to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after he had at least two catches in each of the team's previous five games prior to Week 9. The tight end did play a season-high 53 offensive snaps with Travis Kelce being limited to just 18 snaps on offense as a result of an ankle injury. If Kelce is forced to be limited or even miss the team's Week 11 matchup with Arizona, Gray would stand to operate as the team's primary tight end in his place.

The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

The rookie wideout scored his first career touchdown by beating the cornerback on a stutter-go for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With Josh Downs still getting comfortable and learning the offense following Tuesday's acquisition from the Colts, Allen maintained a significant role on offense, playing 22 of 64 offensive snaps. Once Downs progresses from the 10 snaps he played against Atlanta, it will be interesting to see if Allen can push Xavier Worthy (zero catches on three targets across 56 snaps on Sunday) for a larger piece of the outside receiver role in Kansas City's offense.

Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

Making his Chiefs debut following three days of practice after arriving via trade from the Colts on Tuesday, Downs looked right at home in the Patrick Mahomes-led offense. The young wideout fully capitalized on the upgrade he saw at quarterback, finishing third in receptions, receiving yards and targets right out of the gate and adding his second touchdown of the season on a difficult 18-yard catch just before halftime. Downs' immediate chemistry with Mahomes is highly welcome news for fantasy managers, and he'll aim to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

Rice led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in receptions and targets on a prolific afternoon for the Chiefs' air attack. Rice didn't get in on the scoring fun of a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes, but he still eclipsed 80 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 3. Rice's level of involvement was encouraging given the debuting Josh Downs drew five targets, keeping the former's prospects bright for a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

Taking advantage of a controlled environment and a fast track at Mercedes-Benz Stadium -- not to mention the presence of the debuting Josh Downs -- Mahomes repeatedly exploited the vulnerabilities of the Falcons defense throughout the afternoon. The legendary signal-caller showed no ill effects from the elbow injury that he'd suffered in Week 9, and he connected with Emmett Johnson (12, six yards), Downs (18 yards), Cyrus Allen (39 yards) and Andrew Armstrong (43 yards) for his quintet of touchdown passes. Mahomes now has multiple scoring strikes and zero interceptions in three straight games, and Sunday's five TD tosses represented a new season high. Mahomes will take 2,385 passing yards and a 19:4 TD:INT into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

Delane has been given the green light to return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury. The rookie first-rounder will likely return to his starting role at outside cornerback opposite Nohl Williams, while Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace provide depth at the position.

Fatukasi was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice before downgrading to a DNP on Thursday. The defensive lineman capped off Week 11 prep with a full session Friday but remains questionable for Sunday's divisional bout. If Fatukasi cannot suit up, the absence of Tonka Hemingway (stinger) means Thomas Booker and Tim Keenan will likely start alongside nose tackle Adam Butler for Sunday's game.

Hemingway did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions as he continues to deal with a stinger injury he likely suffered in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. With Hemingway ruled out and Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) listed as questionable, Thomas Booker is currently the only healthy defensive end for the Raiders as they head into a divisional bout.
The veteran kicker was able to practice Friday, which should make him a little better than 50/50 to kick against Denver. If he's unable to, Gay would likely be replaced by Kansei Matsuzawa.

"We still have some conversations to have, so we'll see," Bowers said. With the tight end already slated to carry a questionable tag into the weekend, his own comments don't provide added clarity about whether he'll suit up Sunday. The Raiders may wait until closer to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff before making a final call on Bowers' status. Jack Bech was the big winner in terms of playing time and targets after Bowers left last Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

An ankle injury has sidelined Booker for each of the Raiders' last two games. However, his full session Wednesday indicates that he's recovered from his injury and on track to play in Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Broncos. Booker has accumulated 13 tackles (nine solo) across seven regular-season games.

Paye made an early exit in the second half of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks with a neck injury. The linebacker did not return to the contest, but the issue does not seem to have been serious. Paye is healthy and appears ready to log consistent full practices throughout Week 11 prep.

Thornton is healthy again after sitting out the team's Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to a back injury. However, it is still unlikely that the 23-year-old plays in Sunday's matchup versus the Broncos, as Thornton had been a healthy scratch every week since returning from injured reserve in late October prior to Week 10.

Chinn continues to put up consistent tackling numbers, as he's now logged at least seven stops in six straight games. The veteran safety has played all but one of Las Vegas' defensive snaps this season. He's up to 72 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two recovered fumbles through 10 contests.

Walker, Nakobe Dean and Maxx Crosby all had eight tackles Sunday to co-lead the team. Walker added a fumble recovery on the second play of the game that helped set up a Raiders touchdown. The veteran linebacker has remained productive in his first season with Las Vegas following four years in Green Bay. Walker has 80 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, and two recovered fumbles though 10 contests on the campaign.

Dean tied for the team lead in stops with Maxx Crosby and Quay Walker. Nonetheless, the veteran linebacker saw his five-game streak of double-digit tackles come to an end. Dean did contribute his first recovered fumble of the season when he scooped up a ball that was turned over by Seattle QB Drew Lock in the fourth quarter. Dean is tied with Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton for the NFL lead with 107 tackles, though Denver has played one fewer game.

Crosby tied for the team lead with his season-high eight stops. Among those tackles, four went for a loss, including a fourth-quarter sack of Drew Lock. After registering just a half-sack over six games from Week 2 to Week 7, Crosby has since finished with exactly 1.0 sacks in each of his past three contests. He's at 5.0 sacks overall through 10 games as he seeks a fifth NFL campaign with double-digit sacks.

Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.

Young has suited up in each of the Raiders' 10 games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams. He's seen single-digit snaps on offense in five straight games and has posted a collective 2-36-0 receiving line on three targets on the campaign.

Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25 receiving yards. Though Mendoza will get some more favorable matchups over the Raiders' final seven games, Nailor will be difficult to count on for production. Even while Kirk Cousins served as the starting quarterback for Las Vegas before being traded to the Vikings last week, Nailor was limited to just 14 receptions for 122 yards and one touchdown on 28 targets through eight appearances.

Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.

Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. On a positive note, Mendoza didn't turn the ball over, and he also recorded his first touchdown as a pro on a 10-yard run on the Raiders' opening offensive possession. He'll seek to build on the initial start of his career next Sunday at Denver.

Aside from a 25-carry outburst in Week 8 at the Jets, Washington has logged 54 rushes along with four catches in nine appearances, which amounts to 6.4 touches per game. Despite that number, he continues to eat into the overall backfield picture, as lead runner Ashton Jeanty failed to tally double-digit rushes for a fourth straight contest Sunday. Washington should retain a modest role alongside Jeanty next Sunday at Denver.

After reaching the 10-carry threshold in each of the first six games of the season, Jeanty has failed to do so in four straight contests, and he also has fallen shy of 30 rushing yards in six consecutive outings. Rookie RB Mike Washington continued to split the backfield with Jeanty in Week 10, turning his nine touches into 27 yards from scrimmage. Considering recent trends, Jeanty is difficult to trust for consistent production without a boost in work.

Waxter ended Week 11 prep with consecutive limited sessions after being a non-participant Wednesday. If Waxter cannot suit up for Sunday's game, Deane Leonard is set to be the only reserve cornerback behind starters Cam Hart, Donte Jackson and Tarheeb Still (ankle).

Shelley did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions. The cornerback likely sustained his ankle injury in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens. In the reserve cornerback's absence, Deane Leonard could see snaps at slot cornerback if Tarheeb Still (ankle) does not suit up for Sunday's game.
Williamson ended Week 11 prep with consecutive DNPs. The strong safety remains sidelined with a calf injury he sustained in Week 8 against the Rams.

Eboigbe was unable to play against the Ravens this past Monday due to an ankle injury. He ended Week 11 prep with a full practice Friday, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. His return means there will be less rotational snaps at defensive end for rookie fifth-rounder Nick Barrett.

Still was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to an ankle injury. His late addition to the injury report isn't a great sign ahead of Sunday's game, and if he's unable to play, then Deane Leonard and Genesis Smith would both be in line for more snaps in the Chargers' secondary.

Henley was unable to practice all week, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said Friday that the fourth-year linebacker has been working through knee soreness since Monday's win against the Ravens, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. Denzel Perryman and Marlowe Wax figure to be the top candidates to start at inside linebacker alongside Del'Shawn Phillips in the absence of Henley, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Thompson has been sidelined by a hamstring injury and has not seen regular-season action since Week 2 against the Raiders. If he's ruled out for Sunday's game, then the rookie fourth-rounder's next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.

"Generally, my expecation is [Hampton] is our leading ball carrier every week...I knew based on his last two practice weeks, we were feeling like he was going to have a breakout performance at any given time," McDaniel said Friday. That breakout game took place Thursday against the Ravens, when Hampton turned 22 carries into a season-high 105 yards and a touchdown in a 23-20 win for the Chargers. With the Chargers getting extra time to rest, Hampton's stock is trending up heading into Week 12 against the Jets, whose defense ranks 30th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3) and 29th in rushing touchdowns allowed (13).

The tight end is still in the concussion protocol, so he'll be up against it to clear the final hurdles, especially after the Chargers played Monday night against Baltimore. If Kolar is ruled out, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden should handle most of the tight-end duties for the Bolts.

McConkey, who didn't record any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms and was inactive in Week 10, has been able to practice in a limited fashion thus far this week, but thanks to his official 'questionable' designation, his status will need to be tracked in advance of Sunday's 4:05 ET kickoff. If McConkey is limited or out versus New York, Tre' Harris could maintain a key role in the Chargers' pass-catching corps alongside fellow WR Quentin Johnston.

In a game where Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett dropped back 51 times, there were no shortage of opportunities for the Chargers to rush the passer, and Tomlinson came away with the best single-game sack total of his nine-plus year career so far. He has taken on a larger role on the defensive line than 2025 third-rounder Jamaree Caldwell in recent weeks, and only Teair Tart played as many snaps on the Chargers' defensive front as Tomlinson did (36) in Week 10.

Phillips was in the right place at the right time when a Jacoby Brissett pass bounced off the helmet of rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane in the second quarter, and the turnover set up a Chargers touchdown that put the team ahead 17-7. His tackle total was also his highest going back to Week 18 of the 2023 season with the Ravens. With that said, his role in the Chargers' defense is still not big enough to warrant IDP consideration in most formats.

Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.

Njoku's snap count was predictably capped as he returned from a six-game absence due to a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. With another week under his belt to get back up to speed, Njoku could be more involved in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, squeezing Gadsden out of the game plan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (one), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell appear to be falling into rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown. Mitchell has logged four carries or fewer in three of his last four outings, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role on offense heading into the Chargers' Week 11 home tilt against the Jets on Sunday.

The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally also was a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert made a significant contribution himself to cap off Los Angeles' opening drive of the game, taking off when he couldn't find anyone open and recording a 22-yard rushing touchdown for the first points of the night. The game also marked Herbert's first interception-free performance of the season and gives the beleaguered Chargers' air attack something to hang its collective hat on heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.
Awosika will suit up Monday for the first time since Week 2, when he suffered an injury to his fibula. He should slide back into his starting role at left guard.

Pipkins has been sidelined since Week 1, but he had his 21-day practice window opened Thursday and was listed as questionable heading into Monday. Assuming he can continue practicing in Week 11 without issue, Pipkins could be activated ahead of the Chargers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Jets. Once reinstated, Pipkins could settle back in as the team's starting left guard.

injuries.evidence: Now on injured reserve, he will be required to miss at least four games before being eligible to return.
injuries.detail: Taylor is battling an ankle injury and was ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with Baltimore. Now on injured reserve, he will be required to miss at least four games before being eligible to return.

Nacua is expected to miss "a couple of months" after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his MCL, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. With Nacua and Davante Adams (hamstring, IR) sidelined for Week 10 against the Cardinals, Mumpfield operated as the Rams' WR1 for that contest and finished with three catches (on four targets) for 81 yards in a 34-6 win for Los Angeles. The Rams are "hopeful" that Adams will return soon, but if he's not activated from injured reserve ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers, then Mumpfield would lead Los Angels' wide receiver group that also includes Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.

There was some hope that the veteran pass catcher could be back after the Rams' Week 11 bye, but while McVay indicated that Adams has "been attacking his rehab like crazy, and is excited to be able to get back out there," he acknowledged a return on his part for the team's Nov. 25 game against Green Bay isn't in the cards. With that in mind, McVay  said "there is a possibility for (him to return for the) game after the Packers." As a result, Dec. 3 against the Chiefs would be Adams' next chance to return to a WR corps that will be without Puka Nacua, who will undergo MCL surgery and is out for "a couple months." In the meantime, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith are the team's healthy WRs during the top duo's ongoing absence.

Even if Ferguson is moved back to the active roster, coach Sean McVay's comments indicate the tight end still won't be ready to play coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. His activation would at least keep him off season-ending injured reserve, but his near-term availability remains uncertain until the Rams signal he's ready for game action. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) likely done for the remainder of the regular season following MCL surgery, Ferguson and Davante Adams (hamstring) are needed badly in this offense.

Given that timetable, Nacua -- who is already on injured reserve -- could be out for the rest of the regular season, a huge blow to the Rams' pass-catching corps going forward. In his continued absence, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith are the team's healthy options at WR, though fellow starter Davante Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return in Week 12, following the team's bye.

Garrett was cleared to play in Week 10 after working through a knee injury. The low snap count was more due to the fact that the Cardinals posted only 35 offensive snaps while recording a 17:37 time of possession. The Rams are on a bye for Week 11, so Garrett's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

Lake recorded at least six tackles in each of the first nine games of the regular season, but he had only two stops in Week 10 despite playing every defensive snap. The fifth-year defensive back is up to 65 tackles (38 solo), 11 pass defenses (including three interceptions) and two forced fumbles through 10 regular-season games heading into the Week 11 bye.

Klare has been a healthy inactive on three occasions this season, but he's now suited up in three straight games while the Rams have been short on pass-catching options due to injuries to tight end Terrance Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) and wideouts Puka Nacua (knee), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back). Despite those personnel losses, Klare has still struggled to carve out meaningful playing time, as fellow tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are all regarded as superior blockers and have been prioritized ahead of him. The rookie second-round pick out of Ohio State still has yet to draw a target through his first seven NFL games.

With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) inactive, Daniels' 46 snaps were two fewer than Konata Mumpfield for the team lead at receiver for the Rams. Mumpfield led the group in targets (four), catches (three) and yards (81), and only Xavier Smith (2-40-1) joined him as wide receivers to catch more than one pass from Matthew Stafford against Arizona while the Rams relied heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Daniels' playing time isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

Despite both Puka Nacua (toe/knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being sidelined, Atwell still played just 16 of 76 offensive snaps versus Arizona and ran 15 routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks. Atwell played behind both Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at receiver for Los Angeles.

Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

McManus' Sunday performance extends his perfect streak with a Rams' special teams unit that desperately needed consistency at kicker. He's now 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-14 on PATs after five regular-season contests as a Ram in 2026.

Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

The starting center is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury. Shelton will likely be placed on injured reserve while he recovers. Dylan McMahon (knee, IR) also sustained an injury in the Rams' Week 10 win over the Cardinals, leaving Beaux Limmer to finish out the contest at center and to likely fill in as the starter for the foreseeable future.

injuries.evidence: The injury is severe enough for McMahon to require a stint on IR, so he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, with his next chance to play being Week 16 against the Seahawks on Christmas Day.
injuries.detail: McMahon suffered a knee injury during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. The injury is severe enough for McMahon to require a stint on IR, so he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, with his next chance to play being Week 16 against the Seahawks on Christmas Day. With Coleman Shelton nursing a hamstring injury, the Rams may have to turn to other options like David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer to fill in at center for the time being.

With the Rams down both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) for the first time this season, Smith operated as the fourth receiver against Arizona, playing nine of 76 offensive snaps. His 22-yard touchdown in the second quarter was the first of Smith's career. Based on his small amount of playing time and routes run, Smith's 12-point PPR day isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

Stafford didn't let the fact he was without top wideouts Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) deter him from a very fantasy-friendly performance, as the reigning NFL MVP tossed at least three TD passes for the fourth time this season. Stafford connected with the unlikely trio of Tyler Higbee (five yards), Xavier Smith (22 yards) and Davis Allen (19 yards) for his scoring strikes, and the quarterback's 9.6 yards per attempt was his second-highest figure of the season. Stafford, who'll have a chance to further build chemistry with his current wideouts during the Week 11 bye, could have Adams back for a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25, as reports earlier Sunday indicated the talented wideout is targeting that game for his return.

Williams was held well under 4.0 yards per carry for the third consecutive game, but Sunday's performance was particularly alarming in that he averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per carry. In contrast, Blake Corum (17-100-1) and Ronnie Rivers (15-81-0, albeit in garbage time) both had multiple productive runs on the way to efficient afternoons, making Williams' struggles stand out all the more. With Corum particularly playing well in the last several weeks, Williams could be relegated to a clear complementary role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home showdown with the Packers on Nov. 25, following a Week 11 bye.

Simpson upgraded to a limited participant in Friday's practice after missing consecutive sessions to start Week 11 prep. The reserve cornerback remains unlikely to suit up, but Friday's partial session gives the 26-year-old a chance to be active on game day.

Pinion did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions. The punter likely sustained his groin injury in the Dolphins' Week 10 loss to the Colts. Jack Browning is set to be elevated from the practice squad ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills to take over punting duties.

Meyer suffered a stinger against the Colts in Week 10, but his full practice Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's AFC East game. He would likely start at center for a second consecutive week if Aaron Brewer (concussion) is not cleared to play.

Brewer was unable to play against the Colts in Week 10 while in the league's concussion protocol. He logged a full practice Friday, but he won't be allowed to suit up Sunday unless he passes an evaluation by an independent neurologist, which would get him out of protocol. Andrew Meyer would likely start at center if Brewer is not available.

Brents' practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday due to a neck injury, but his full session Friday was enough for the fourth-year defensive back to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt. Brents has accumulated 33 tackles (18 solo), one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

Wayne will miss a second straight game due to a quadriceps injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29. In his absence, Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert will serve as the Dolphins' rotational wide receivers behind Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell.
The rookie wideout is averaging 1.5 catches for 18.5 yards per game this season and is not in the conversation to start for fantasy teams with both Caleb Douglas and Malik Washington healthy.

Douglas was managed during the practice week, but he's good to go for his normal every-down role Sunday against Buffalo. With the Dolphins installed as 16.5-point underdogs, Miami is projected to throw a ton in comeback mode. Douglas is a tough click for fantasy with Kyle McCord under center.

Trader opened the week as a non-participant in practice after suffering groin and shoulder injuries during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts last Sunday. Kyle Louis and Julius Wood may see more time in his place if Trader does indeed miss Week 11. Trader has 45 tackles (23 solo) and three pass breakups, including one interception, through nine 2026 regular-season games.

Baker managed to practice in full for a second straight session Wednesday, suggesting he's trending in the right direction as the Dolphins begin their Week 11 preparations. For now, he's still on the reserve/PUP list as Sunday's matchup against the Bills approaches.

injuries.evidence: Phillips was recently placed on injured reserve with a season-ending biceps injury sustained in Week 10 versus the Colts.
injuries.detail: Phillips was recently placed on injured reserve with a season-ending biceps injury sustained in Week 10 versus the Colts. The 22-year-old ends his season with 28 tackles (11 solo) through nine games. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper are top candidates to see more reps at defensive tackle as the season continues.

Brooks was able to register at least nine takedowns for the fourth straight game and seventh time overall this season. The linebacker was also able to strip Colts running back Jonathan Taylor in the first quarter, but offensive lineman Dalton Tucker was able to jump on the loose ball. Brooks is now up to 84 total tackles (38 solo) while also adding two passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine contests to open the 2026 season.

Rodriguez finished with fewer than eight takedowns for just the third time this season, and his one tackle was a season low for the rookie. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (36 solo), including a 1.0 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over nine contests so far during his rookie campaign.

Taaffe was able to register at least six stops for the third straight game and sixth time overall this season. The safety's biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter, when he jumped in front of a short pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, securing his third interception of the year. On the year, Taaffe has compiled 53 total tackles (27 solo), three interceptions and a forced fumble over nine contests so far.

Johnson was able to secure an interception for the second straight week, jumping in front of a pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in the third quarter, ultimately returning the interception for a 59-yard touchdown. The cornerback has now registered 46 total tackles (24 solo), four passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine games this season.

Coleman couldn't get on the same page as QB Kyle McCord, who made his first NFL regular-season appearance. In fact, Coleman has been quiet inefficient regardless of who has thrown him the ball this year, as he has just nine receptions on 27 targets through nine games. Two of his nine catches have been touchdowns, but he's not getting enough touches to be a trustworthy fantasy option.

Cook served as the team's No. 2 option at quarterback behind Kyle McCord in the team's 24-22 loss to the Colts in Week 10, with Malik Willis (abdomen) being placed on injured reserve prior to the contest. Cook reverted to the practice squad Monday, but he has now officially become a member of the team's active roster ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

injuries.evidence: Biggers suffered a lateral meniscus tear in Week 10, and he will now miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign while on IR.
injuries.detail: Biggers suffered a lateral meniscus tear in Week 10, and he will now miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign while on IR. Fellow defensive lineman Jordan Phillips (biceps) was also placed on IR on Tuesday, and as a result, Kenneth Grant will operate as the team's top dog at defensive tackle moving forward this season.

Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-3 yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.

Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.

Per Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, Hafley noted on that subject Monday, "We will see how he feels. If he needs surgery, he will have surgery," while adding that if the QB does undergo a procedure, it wouldn't "necessarily" be season ending. In any case, the earliest Willis can come off IR is Week 14, with Kyle McCord and Brady Cook currently available to handle Miami's signal-caller duties.

Bartholomew was targeted four times in Week 10 for three catches, 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end received more than one target in only one other game this season, Week 5, when Hockenson went down after two offensive snaps. While Bartholomew has proven himself a red-zone threat, Hockenson should return to seeing most of the tight end volume in Sunday's contest.

Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

Rodgers popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a quad injury. His practice reps were also limited in Friday's session, and his status for Sunday's contest may not be officially known until the Vikings announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. Rookie fifth-rounder Charles Demmings and Zemaiah Vaughn would likely be the top candidates to start opposite James Pierre if Rodgers is not cleared to play against San Francisco.

Van Ginkel's practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday while managing a quadriceps injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Packers. He was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for the veteran edge rusher to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. In Van Ginkel's four outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, he has accumulated 14 tackles (eight solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

Cashman will end up missing one game (Week 10 against the Packers) while in the league's concussion protocol, and his return means Ivan Pace will revert to a rotational role at inside linebacker for Sunday's contest. Cashman has accumulated 76 tackles (41 solo), including a career-high-tying 4.5 sacks, seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery across eight regular-season games.

The quarterback lost his job to Kirk Cousins and will continue to manage a hamstring injury. Murray's availability will only matter moving forward if something happens to Cousins, either performance or injury related. Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer remain on the 53-man roster as backup options.

After sitting out last Sunday against Green Bay and then logging limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Hockenson is ready to return against San Francisco in a potential playoff preview. His lack of a designation puts Minnesota's top tight end in position to reclaim his usual role in the passing game that now has Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Hockenson is a TE1 for fantasy purposes.

The Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times in Week 10, with Wilson taking down the Packers quarterback for a six-yard loss early in the second quarter. Wilson has logged at least 0.5 sacks in three of his last four outings, and the veteran linebacker is up to 57 tackles (30 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one pass defense through nine regular-season games.

injuries.evidence: Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers.
injuries.detail: Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.

Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.

Thus, the Vikings are expecting Addison to recover fully before the four games required of an IR stint, but in any case he will miss some time due to the thumb injury he suffered in practice last Friday and sidelined him this past Sunday at Green Bay. With Addison out of the lineup, Minnesota will be relying on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price, Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver.

All three of Reichard's field goals came from fewer than 40 yards out in the contest. The return of Kirk Cousins allowed Minnesota's offense to surge to its highest touchdown total since Week 1, the team's first bout against the Packers. Reichard is now 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and remains perfect at 13-for-13 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison now is expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position in Minnesota's offense for the time being.

Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Jones' upside will remain limited while working in a timeshare with Mason, but he's still got some utility heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.

Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. The Vikings' passing game didn't need to over-extend itself, however, as the defense sacked Jordan Love eight times in another dominant performance. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.

In Kirk Cousins' return to the Vikings, Jefferson led the team in catches, targets and receiving yards, although Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew were on the other end of the QB's two touchdown passes. The nine grabs and 13 targets were season highs for Jefferson, while the yardage total was his best showing since Week 5. Despite a disappointing 40-467-4 line on 64 targets through eight games, the star wideout's outlook for the rest of the year is pointed up heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

Metellus was added to the Vikings' practice report Friday due to a shoulder issue, but the injury won't prevent the seventh-year pro from suiting up for Sunday's NFC North showdown. He has 58 tackles (29 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.
doubtful

Maye was knocked out of Week 10 action on the first possession of this past Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich. He already was expected to miss multiple games as a result of the injury, but with a diagnosis now available, he's now in rehab mode until further notice. A return at some point down the stretch likely will depend on the Patriots remaining in the playoff race, but for the time being Tommy DeVito will be under center in place of Maye.

Week 10 was the third time this season that Elliss posted double-digit stops, and he ended up co-leading the Patriots in tackles with safety Kevin Byard. Through 10 regular-season games, Elliss has accumulated 75 tackles (37 solo), including 1.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Elliss's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Byard picked off a Jared Goff pass intended for Jameson Williams in the end zone late in the second quarter, which halted the Lions' red zone drive in its tracks. It was the first time this season that Byard posted double-digit stops, and each of the veteran safety's two interceptions on the year have come over his last three outings. He enters the Week 11 bye with 53 tackles (26 solo) and five pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle injury that he sustained in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown of Larison's NFL career, although he's firmly entrenched as the team's RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.
